solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Defeat by narrow margin for the twerp

parts.note: to pip someone is to beat them narrowly, as in pipped at the post
a narrow squeak is an escape or win by the slimmest of margins

explanation.surface: A sports report sneering at a weakling who loses by a whisker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defeat by narrow margin' reads as one idea but splits into two pieces, with 'by' joining them and 'for the' leading to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal insults for an insignificant, irritating little person.

clue.text: French city is substandard?

parts.note: read as sub plus standard: par is the standard, as in golf, and the word is sits sub (under) it in this down light

explanation.surface: A sniffy remark that the French capital is not up to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'substandard' is read as 'sub' (under) plus 'standard' (PAR, as in golf): in this down light IS sits under PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of France is its best-known city, so a French city is a fair definition by example.

clue.text: Shop ordered pepper primarily, with extreme loathing for salt

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so the letters of shop are put in a new order
primarily means taking only the first letter of the word pepper

parts.note: extreme loathing is hate

explanation.surface: A shopper orders pepper but has a violent dislike of salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns SHOP into PHOS. 'salt' looks like table salt, but chemists use the word for any compound made from an acid and a base.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical salt of phosphoric acid, used in fertilisers, is an example of a salt in the chemical sense.

clue.text: Shot of tequila about right — this supposedly lucky?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the letter for right
shot means wrecked or knocked about, so the letters of of tequila are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a shot of tequila might bring them luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a measure of drink, but it is the anagram signal: OF TEQUILA becomes QUATEFOIL, and 'about' wraps that around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-leaved design echoes the four-leaf clover, a traditional charm for good fortune.

clue.text: Event is confined to school in case of earthquake

indicators.note: in means the built piece sits between the outer letters
case of means only the outer shell, the first and last letters, of earthquake
confined to means the word is is held inside the school word

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A safety notice telling pupils to stay in school during an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a place of learning but a group of whales, and 'case of earthquake' means just its outside letters, the two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single incident or occurrence in a series of happenings, so it is a synonym of event.

clue.text: A half and a whole fish for author

indicators.note: a half means only the first half of the fish name is kept

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A recipe or fishmonger's order for one and a half fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' does double duty: half of KIPPER (KIP) and the whole of LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling wrote The Jungle Book, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Nag beginning to shiver, then in need of a blanket?

indicators.note: beginning to means take the opening letter of shiver

parts.note: someone in need of a blanket is cold

explanation.surface: A horse starts shivering and needs a rug thrown over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a horse, which suits the blanket, but it is a verb meaning to keep on at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag and to scold both mean to rebuke or find fault with someone persistently.

clue.text: Basic construction abandoned

definitions.meaning: a simple hut or outbuilding, a basic structure
cast off or discarded, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: A rough building project that was given up.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a simple garden hut; the other is the past tense of casting something off.

clue.text: In abeyance — everything nasty then?

definitions.meaning: postponed or held in reserve for later
if everything is nasty, then zero things are pleasant: a letter for nothing followed by a word for pleasant, a cryptic second reading

explanation.surface: Plans are on hold, and a gloomy voice asks if all is horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: if everything is nasty there is zero nice, O + NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put in cold storage are postponed or suspended, which is what being in abeyance means.

clue.text: Diameters in circles, most beautiful

indicators.note: going in circles means the letters of diameters are spun around into a new order

explanation.surface: A geometer's rapture over diameters drawn inside circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in circles' suits the diameters, but it signals that DIAMETERS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy is informal for lovely or gorgeous, and the superlative form means loveliest of all.

clue.text: Film from Japan on port wine

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the following piece comes after the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port, often just Rio

indicators.note: film from Japan means the film word is taken away out of Japan

parts.note: J is the international vehicle registration letter for Japan
to pan is to film by swinging the camera across a scene

explanation.surface: A Japanese film shown at a port, followed by a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink beside 'wine' but is a harbour city. 'Film from Japan' removes PAN (to film by sweeping the camera) from JAPAN, leaving JA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish red or white from the region of the same name, an example of wine.

clue.text: Rough price, semi-wrong?

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of price and semi are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A rough estimate of the price that is half incorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough figure is approximate rather than exact, which is what inexact or imprecise means.

clue.text: Second note scrawled on pictures

indicators.note: scrawled means written messily, so the letters of on pictures are jumbled

explanation.surface: A second memo has been scribbled on top of some pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second note' looks like a further memo, but in music it is the second degree of a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: In the major or minor scale, the degree just above the tonic is the second note.

clue.text: Teaching time during winter months

indicators.note: during means the letters sit inside the run of the words winter months

explanation.surface: Schools are in session through the winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A school year is split into periods of teaching, each called a term.

clue.text: A close game?

parts.note: close here means nearby rather than tight: a match between neighbouring teams

explanation.surface: A tightly fought match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' wants to mean a tight score; it means geographically near, as when two teams from the same town meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A derby between neighbouring clubs is a fixture played close to home for both sides.

clue.text: Those cheering for pixies taken aback a bit

indicators.note: taken aback means read backwards

parts.note: supporters of elves are elf fans

explanation.surface: Fans of pixies are a little surprised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise but signals reversal, and 'a bit' is not 'slightly' but a horse's bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A snaffle is a simple jointed mouthpiece for a horse, a kind of bit.

clue.text: Promise head of parliamentarian in slaughter, fighting with blades

indicators.note: in means the promise and initial go inside the slaughter word

parts.note: to slay is to slaughter
giving your word is making a promise

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of parliamentarian

explanation.surface: An MP pledges to take part in a massacre with swords.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing or duelling with swords is combat using blades.

clue.text: Good womaniser entertaining good, keen follower

parts.note: pi is short for pious, so good in crosswords

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the second good inside the womaniser

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man, a rake
pi is short for pious, so good in crosswords

explanation.surface: A decent rake has a pious guest and a devoted fan.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A groupie is an ardent fan who follows a band or celebrity around.

clue.text: Someone driven to succeed in exam on difficult genre

parts.note: to pass is to succeed in an exam

indicators.note: difficult means the letters of genre are made awkward and rearranged

explanation.surface: An ambitious student sitting an exam on a hard literary genre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Someone driven' looks like an ambitious type, but means a person being driven in a car. 'difficult' turns GENRE into ENGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is carried in a vehicle by somebody else at the wheel.

clue.text: Chance for first performance

definitions.meaning: a premiere, the first night of a show

explanation.surface: An opportunity to appear at a premiere.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a vacancy or chance; the other is a show's first night.

clue.text: Tastelessly showy houses nauseating at first — so decorate!

indicators.note: houses means the garish word holds the initial inside it

parts.note: garish means gaudy, tastelessly showy

indicators.note: at first means the first letter of nauseating

explanation.surface: Gaudy homes are sickening, so prettify them!
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like dwellings, but it is the verb: GARISH contains N.
explanation.definitionFit: To garnish a dish is to embellish or trim it, so it means to adorn.

clue.text: Name evidently forgotten, write "Dolly Vardens" in card

indicators.note: in means the hats go inside the word for a card

parts.note: a card is a joker or wag, a wit
a Dolly Varden is a large brimmed hat, named after a Dickens character

explanation.surface: An instruction to write a puzzling phrase on a greetings card, its sender's name forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' means a funny person (WIT), not stationery; Dolly Vardens are big hats, named after a Dickens character.
explanation.definitionFit: People say this word when they cannot remember what a thing is called.

clue.text: Film wife, if not the rear!

indicators.note: not means the word if is to be left out of the word wife

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A wife, told to stop being a backside, in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wife, if not' is literal: write WIFE without IF to leave WE. 'the rear' is a ship's STERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy picture set on the American frontier is a genre of movie.

clue.text: Duck joint

definitions.meaning: to duck is to plunge or drop down quickly
a seedy bar or club, informally a joint

explanation.surface: A bird and a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a sudden plunge downward; the other is a disreputable drinking place.

clue.text: Roar from engine, as low revs regularly turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of revs

explanation.surface: An engine roars when the low revs are turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is not slow but the noise of cattle, MOO. With RV from 'revs', 'turned up' reads MOORV upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the imitative word for the throaty noise a revving motor makes.

clue.text: Adopt the habits of one's wife or husband?

definitions.text: Adopt the habits of one's wife or husband?

parts.words: Adopt the habits of one's wife or husband?
parts.note: habits here means clothing, not customs: wearing your spouse's clothes

explanation.surface: A spouse picks up their partner's behaviour over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' wants to be routines; it means garments, as in a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear clothing usually worn by the opposite sex is to dress in a partner's garments.

clue.text: Fight a bit

explanation.surface: A short scuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an informal fight; the other is a small leftover piece.

clue.text: Latin year's ending coming up — so soon?

indicators.note: ending coming up means the last letter of the Latin word moves higher in this down light

parts.note: anno is Latin for in the year, as in Anno Domini

explanation.surface: The Latin year is ending soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending coming up' lifts the final O of ANNO one place higher.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic word for shortly or presently.

clue.text: Cook is anyone going beyond starter of lentils with onions

indicators.note: going beyond means the rearranged letters come after the lentil initial
starter of means the opening letter of lentils
cook means doctor or falsify, so the letters of is anyone are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef asks who will go past lentils to an onion dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' turns IS ANYONE into YONNAISE, which follows L.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish described this way, after the city of Lyon, is cooked with sliced onions.

clue.text: Boy's name? Got it!

definitions.meaning: the radio reply meaning message received and understood

explanation.surface: Someone confirms they have caught a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common male first name and also radio slang for received.

clue.text: Country needing soldiers behind you

indicators.note: behind means the soldiers come after the old word for you

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
men are soldiers, other ranks

explanation.surface: A nation needs troops to back you up.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is a nation at the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Alluring snare, perfect celebration backfiring

parts.note: to hone is to perfect or sharpen a skill

indicators.note: backfiring means the celebration word goes into reverse

parts.note: a party is a celebration

explanation.surface: A perfect party goes horribly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' is a verb, HONE, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sexual-lure sting used by spies or journalists to entrap a target.
